title: What Moved India's Prices in September: Onion, Food and the New CPI
source_short: MoSPI · Consumer Price Index (base 2024) · September 2026, provisional
source: Ministry of Statistics and Programme Implementation (National Statistics Office): Consumer Price Index (base 2024=100), press release for September 2026, PIB PRID 2322244, 12 Oct 2026, Annexures I to IV; first release of the new series, PRID 2227012, 12 Feb 2026; every all-India item, and food and onion by state, from MoSPI's eSankhyiki portal, read 14 and 15 Oct 2026. Reserve Bank of India: Resolution of the Monetary Policy Committee and Governor's Statement, 7 Oct 2026. Ministry of Consumer Affairs, Food and Public Distribution: onion buffer release, PIB PRID 2303587, 26 Aug 2026. September figures are provisional.

chapters.title: Beyond food: jewellery, travel and fuel

vo: In September, onion cost {onion:say} more than a year before: more than double.
Prices across India were up {headline:say} on a year earlier, the highest this year.
Over the year, prices rose the most in one place: Puducherry.
These are September's provisional figures, from the official tables.

vo: In January, onion cost {onion_jan:say} less than a year earlier.
By June, it cost {onion_jun_m:say} more.
Then it climbed fast, through July and August.
In September, onion was {onion:say} above a year before.

vo: Here is what that means in the index.
A year earlier, onion's index stood at {onion_sep25:say}.
This September it was {onion_sep:say}: more than double.

vo: Not everything rose. Potato was down {potato:say} on a year before, and tomato {tomato:say}.

scenes.title: What the government said on 26 August

tiles.caption: a kilo: the retail price the ministry announced
lakh tonnes: estimated crop of 2025 to 2026, close to the year before
lakh tonnes bought for the buffer, of {buffer_target:n} planned

scenes.note: Ministry of Consumer Affairs, Food and Public Distribution, press release of 26 August 2026.
scenes.source: Ministry of Consumer Affairs · onion buffer release · PIB, 26 Aug 2026
vo: By the twenty-sixth of August, the government said it had begun releasing onions from its buffer stock.
It announced retail sales at {sale_price:say} a kilo, and called supplies comfortable.
It said onion prices typically rise in the festive season.

scenes.text: Onion prices increased by about 85 per cent by end-September over end-June, driven by low rabi stocks and concerns over kharif arrivals amid uneven rainfall. As a result, the increase during August-September is sharper than the usual seasonal pick-up.
scenes.by: Reserve Bank of India, Governor's Statement
scenes.source: RBI · Governor's Statement, 7 Oct 2026, footnote 13 · rbi.org.in
vo: Six weeks later, the RBI gave its reading.
It pointed to low rabi stocks and worries over kharif arrivals, amid uneven rain.
And it called the rise sharper than the usual seasonal pick-up.
Its figure compares end-June with end-September, and came before the September index.

Chapter six: villages and cities.

scenes.title: Inflation, rural and urban
scenes.caption: In January the two were almost level: {rural_jan} rural and {urban_jan} urban.

vo: In January, prices in villages and cities rose at almost the same pace.
By September, villages were ahead.
Rural inflation was {rural:say}. Urban, {urban:say}.

Food and drinks weigh more in village baskets: {fw_rural:say}, against {fw_urban:say} in cities.
MoSPI does not say whether the two are linked, and neither do we.

Mizoram was lowest, at {mizoram:say}.

Chapter eight: what the RBI did.

scenes.title: The RBI's repo rate
scenes.caption: Up a quarter point ({bps:n} basis points), five days before September's prices were published.
scenes.source: RBI · Monetary Policy Committee: resolution of 7 Oct 2026 and minutes of the August meeting · rbi.org.in
vo: The repo rate is the rate at which the RBI lends money to banks for short periods.
On the seventh of October, the RBI raised it by a quarter point, to {repo_after:say}.
Its committee voted for the rise unanimously.
That was five days before September's price figures came out.

and {proj_q3:say} for October to December. These are the RBI's projections, not ours.
